title: l3lint canonical payload
description: A commercial card transaction with Level 2 and Level 3 data in l3lint's gateway-neutral shape. Absent and null both mean the value was not sent. Business constraints that a rule checks (positive amount, currency code, field lengths by brand, line-item counts, sequence order) are left to those rules so each problem is reported once.

id.description: The merchant's own reference for the transaction.

transactionDate.description: Date of the transaction; drives rule effective dates.

channel.description: Whether the card was present. Visa asks for a billing postal code when it was not.

card.description: What l3lint knows about the card. Gateways rarely send brand and product, so pass them with --brand and --card-product when they are missing.

brand.description: Card brand. It decides which brand rule packs run.

product.description: Card product. It decides eligibility for enhanced-data rates.

productCode.description: Brand product code such as MBS or MEF.

isFederalGovernment.description: True for a US federal government card, which Visa excludes from Product 3 at some medical MCCs.

last4.description: Last four digits of the card number. Never a full card number.

mcc.description: Merchant category code, 4 digits. Some MCCs are excluded from enhanced-data rates.

name.description: Merchant name. The data quality rules flag line descriptions that repeat it.

taxId.description: Merchant tax ID. One processor lists it as required for Mastercard Level 2.

reference.description: Customer code, often the buyer's purchase order number.

indicator.description: Whether the sale is taxable or exempt. Visa wants an explicit exempt flag, not a bare zero tax amount.

rate.description: Tax rate as a fraction: 0.07 means 7%.

exemptionId.description: Tax registration or exemption ID. Amex asks for it when the sale is exempt.

discount.description: Header-level discount. Visa wants 0 when there is none.

freight.description: Freight or shipping amount. Visa wants 0 when nothing ships.

duty.description: Duty amount. Visa wants 0 when there is none.

handling.description: Handling amount. Not part of the transaction total formula; the total check says so when it is above 0.

shipping.description: Where the goods ship from and to.

postalCode.description: Billing postal code, used for address verification.

requestorName.description: Name of the person who placed the order. Amex Level 3 asks for it under structured acquirer profiles.

adviceText.description: Transaction advice text lines. Some processors send at most 4 lines of 40 characters.

sequence.description: 1-based line number. Adapters fill it from array order.

description.description: Item descriptor: the real product or service name.

commodityCode.description: Commodity code, usually an 8-digit UNSPSC code.

unitOfMeasure.description: Unit of measure, such as EA or BX. Mastercard and Amex accept only codes from their lists.

unitCost.description: Unit price before discount. At most 6 decimal places.

discountAmount.description: Discount on this line. Visa wants 0 when there is none.

discountIndicator.description: True when a discount applies to this line.

taxRate.description: Tax rate on this line as a fraction: 0.07 means 7%.

taxable.description: Line tax indicator: true when the line is taxable.

taxTypeCode.description: Processor tax type code for the line.

amountIncludesTax.description: True when total includes the line tax. Absent means false. It changes the arithmetic.

total.description: Line total (extended amount): quantity times unit cost, less the line discount, plus the line tax when amountIncludesTax is true.

debitCreditIndicator.description: debit adds to the total, credit (a return) subtracts from it. Absent means debit.

detailIndicator.description: Visa line-item detail indicator, 1 character. Often set by the processor.
